statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure removes the very price path this score measures. Stress eases to 52 in the elevated band: a second quiet hour passed with no verified new escalation, and Iran's foreign ministry has confirmed that its counterpart will meet Gulf Cooperation Council and Iraqi ministers in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, which adds a de-escalation channel against the still-shut East-West pipeline. Confidence is 85 on a complete evidence set re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three facts support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and the advance was broad, with seven of eight tracked megacaps higher and semiconductor gains spread across ARM, QCOM, INTC and AMD rather than concentrated in one leader. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, roughly eight hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot in the forecast contains a tradeable session and no danger window is published. Third, the geopolitical channel gained a de-escalation vector this weekend rather than only an escalation one: Brent fell 2.81% and WTI 2.37% on Friday on reported Hormuz diplomatic progress, and the Oman meeting is now confirmed for Monday. Stress stays elevated at 52 because the East-West pipeline that carries 4 to 5 million barrels a day remains shut with no published repair timeline, Houthi forces are reported to have taken Mokha and the Perim and Zuqar islands near Bab al-Mandab, and the FOMC decision with projections lands on Wednesday. Those are Stress and Confidence inputs, not Tail inputs, until an observed price path establishes persistent mean-reversion failure.
headline: Eighteen hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, and this hour the balance of evidence tilted slightly toward de-escalation: Iran's foreign ministry confirmed its minister will meet Gulf Cooperation Council and Iraqi counterparts in Oman on Monday to discuss the Strait of Hormuz, the first such gathering since the U.S.-Israeli campaign began, while the East-West pipeline remains shut with substantial satellite-confirmed damage at two pumping stations and no repair timeline.
body:
This hour re-verified the full evidence set against primary sources and found the price picture unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend. The Nasdaq-100 quote page still shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high. VIX remains 15.84, down 11.21%, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, still shows the 2-year at 4.56% and the 10-year at 4.95% with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%, a curve consistent with a tightening path rather than a growth scare.

Friday's participation was broad rather than narrow. Seven of the eight tracked megacaps closed higher, and semiconductor strength was spread across ARM at +4.17%, QCOM at +2.88%, INTC at +2.61% and AMD at +2.49% while NVDA finished essentially flat. Sector gains were similarly distributed across technology, communication services and consumer cyclicals. Breadth of that kind is poor precursor evidence for the squeeze-type one-way structure this Tail score is built to detect, and it is the main reason the conditional path into an eventual reopen is scored as gap exposure rather than trend risk.

The geopolitical picture is the reason Stress remains elevated while Tail stays low, and it moved in two directions this weekend. On the escalation side, Saudi Arabia's 1,200-kilometre East-West pipeline, which carries 4 to 5 million barrels a day or roughly 4 to 5 percent of global supply from Abqaiq to Yanbu, remains shut as a precaution after drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province struck it. Satellite imaging analysis shows clear and substantial impacts at two pumping stations, including particularly extensive fire damage at one, and no restart or repair timeline has been published. Houthi forces are separately reported to have captured Mokha and the Perim and Zuqar islands, moving closer to control of Bab al-Mandab, the alternative route while Hormuz transit is restricted. On the de-escalation side, Iran's foreign ministry has confirmed that its minister will meet Gulf Cooperation Council and Iraqi counterparts in Oman on Monday to discuss the strait, the first such meeting since the campaign against Tehran began, building on an existing Iran-Oman understanding on shipping lanes and mine clearing. Oil closed Friday lower on that news, with WTI marked $100.05, down 2.37%, and Brent $104.61, down 2.81%, even though WTI still ended the week 9.7% higher and the month 20.15% higher.

The macro backdrop is hawkish and largely priced. Friday's inflation print showed headline consumer prices up 0.4% on the month and 3.4% on the year with core at 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast, and market-implied pricing now leans toward a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC, while forecaster surveys remain divided. The Federal Reserve's own calendar confirms that meeting carries both a Summary of Economic Projections and a press conference, which is why it is treated as a structurally multi-stage sequence rather than a single print. None of that sits inside this 24-hour horizon.

The shared Finviz cross-asset context was collected at 13:10 UTC with a partial status and its calendar section unavailable, so at roughly two and a quarter hours old it is stale under the freshness contract and was not relied upon. Its futures, breadth, megacap and semiconductor sections describe the same Friday session already verified independently above and did not contradict it.

Tail is therefore 6. The calibration test for a higher reading is observed persistent directional efficiency or multiple independent current amplifiers, and a closed venue can supply neither. Stress is 52, easing by one point on a quiet hour and a confirmed diplomatic channel while staying elevated on the unresolved pipeline outage, the Red Sea advance and Wednesday's event stack. Confidence is 85, high rather than very high, because the evidence set is complete and freshly verified but contains no live price path at all.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 15:00 UTC on 11 September to 14:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens inside the U.S. afternoon that followed Friday's 12:30 UTC inflation print, with Tail between 13 and 17 in mixed mode and Stress at 81 decaying steadily as the event passed and volatility fell. Tail dropped to 7 at the 21:00 UTC futures halt and has since settled into a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across the final seventeen slots, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress fell monotonically from 81 to 53 across the twenty-four hours, and Confidence held inside the high band throughout, between 85 and 89. No slot in the window reached the 25-point Tail block threshold.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, roughly eight hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then drifts through 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 to a ceiling of 12 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of an eventual reopen. Every slot stays deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published because no slot contains a tradeable session. Stress runs from 52 down to a floor of 48 through the overnight quiet, then edges back to 51 as the Monday Oman meeting on the Strait of Hormuz and the reopen both approach with their outcomes unknown. Confidence decays from 85 to 78 on assessment age alone rather than on any gap in the evidence, and stays inside the high band for all twenty-four slots. The conditional risk being described is a reopen gap, not trend continuation: raising Tail further would require observed shallow or failed retracements, repeated extension, or a contract holding near session extremes, and a closed venue cannot supply any of those.
